analysis.title: Headline Roulette Is Back: MidEast Missiles & AI Angst Spark 'Violent Rotations'
key_insights: Thursday Oct 8 saw a break in the stock, bond and oil correlation regime as separate idiosyncratic shocks hit each market. Goldman's vol desk called it 'violent rotations across the board' driven by geopolitical and AI headlines.

Oil rose over 4% in WTI futures on Mideast escalation. Dated Brent is near war highs, ahead of the futures price. The Houthis hit two Saudi airports, Iran extended tanker attacks into the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, and a tanker was struck off Qatar.

A Trump post saying the US will not attack Iran before the November midterms briefly pushed oil down. Oil did not close lower because Iranian officials are suspicious of Trump's statements and want to avoid a third surprise attack.

The larger oil problem is thin global supply. Reserves are well below pre-war levels. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said 'The supply resilience cushion is scarily thin.' A Gulf of America hurricane also halted some US production.

Refined products, especially diesel, rose sharply this week. Tanker rates are at records, with Middle East to China shipping costing $1.4 million a day on Wednesday. This feeds inflation readings and expectations.

Treasury yields ended lower with the long end outperforming. Yields tested the prior day's highs overnight on oil, then bond buying came in as oil dipped, and again after the OpenAI report. Rate-hike expectations changed very little at the short end.

The Treasury's long-end buyback took a full $6 billion ticket on 20-30 year bonds, with a little under $15 billion tendered. The 30-year auction was described as mediocre, but TD Securities' Molly Brooks said demand held up.
NDX was the biggest loser, its worst day since July, while the Dow was roughly unchanged. Tech was the worst sector, energy the best, and staples were bid.

A report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $20bn below what was previously signaled drove selling across AI stocks. ORCL was slammed, and NeoClouds and optical networking fell about 7%. Ramp data show OpenAI losing share to Anthropic.

Goldman's desk named three other drags on semis and AI: underwhelming Samsung and TSM prints against high expectations, reports that ORCL, AVGO and SCPX plan to tap debt markets, and no update on the China optical ban weighing on COHR, LITE and GLW.

Goldman traders rated activity about 4 out of 10 with flow skewed to sellers. Hedge funds were much better sellers, led by info tech, macro products, comms services and consumer staples. Asset managers were 5% better sellers.

Realized vol had been low until Thursday. That lets vol-control and risk-parity funds hold or add equity exposure. SPX gamma is thick around 7750-7800 per SpotGamma. A jump in realized vol can turn these funds into forced sellers.

Bitcoin fell toward $80,000 on a US government wallet move and the tech selloff. Gold rose modestly and the gold/silver ratio hit about 70x, a two-month high. The dollar swung intraday and ended flat.
RTY outperformed NDX after underperforming in 17 of the last 20 sessions. AAII bull/bear sentiment is back to neutral, which removes the earlier extreme-negative sentiment tailwind.

The author argues that high oil and high real rates are hard on consumers, small businesses and leveraged balance sheets. Strong earnings are not offsetting pressure from rates, energy and capital supply.

geopolitical: Reports on Wednesday said the Pentagon was ordered to prepare Iran attack options for before the midterms.
Iran-backed Houthis struck two Saudi airports and killed three people. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 82 Houthi targets in Yemen.
Iran expanded tanker attacks beyond the Strait of Hormuz into the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Projectiles struck a tanker off northwest Qatar with casualties, per UKMTO.
A reported fire was detected in the Gulf of Oman about 30 nautical miles east of Fujairah, and an oil tanker assembly site near the UAE reportedly exploded.

Trump said on Truth Social that the US will not attack Iran before the November midterms and that talks are productive. Iranian officials are suspicious and want to avoid a third surprise attack, per Axios.
China optical ban: no updates, which weighs on US optical names.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower OpenAI revenue may still leave solid chip demand because Anthropic is gaining share and demand may come from elsewhere. Lower AI spend could also ease Treasury supply competition.
tension_points.bear_case: OpenAI has hundreds of billions in commitments to fulfill and a $20bn revenue shortfall could damp AI demand growth. AI firms are also tapping debt markets.

tension_points.bull_case: The 30-year auction held up and a TD Securities strategist called it a good sign for buyers returning to the long end. Bond buying came in on oil dips.
tension_points.bear_case: The auction was only mediocre and the long bond looks exhausted. Oil-driven inflation could push yields higher and lower AI revenue may mean more debt is needed.
